science_checks.detail: AC is a common incident wavefront perpendicular to both incoming rays. A is on MN while C is still above MN on the second incoming ray, leaving positive CB to travel. The current prose starts the shared clock at A and stops it at B. At that final instant the wavelet at B has zero age; A has age Delta t = CB/v1.

The A-centered lower wavelet has radius AD. D lies on the transmitted A-A2 ray and on the drawn arc. DB touches the arc at D and AD is perpendicular to DB. Both smaller lower wavelets have centers on AB, tangency points on DB and smaller radii consistent with their later starts.

Alpha is drawn in the upper-left sector between A-A1 and the upper normal; beta is drawn in the lower-right sector between A-A2 and the lower normal. Alpha equals angle CAB, beta equals angle ABD, and beta is smaller. Neither is an angle from ray to interface.

ABC is right at C; ADB is right at D; both share AB as hypotenuse. The current English locally identifies CB opposite alpha at A and AD opposite beta at B. Thus CB = AB sin(alpha) = v1 Delta t and AD = AB sin(beta) = v2 Delta t. Their ratio gives sin(alpha)/sin(beta) = v1/v2 = n2/n1 for fixed-frequency phase speeds, consistent with the slower second-medium schematic. No numerical angle, speed, time or index is presented as source data.
